rule.rank: percentile rank = (scores below + half the ties) / population size; the population of an item is every stock holding a score on that item from its registered run (or its published memo)
rule.registered_run: the newest live card in the conveyor's trays whose run holds scores; dry, cancelled and control runs never enter
rule.boundaries: per item, the lowest score that earned each grade today; null where no score earned that grade
rule.comparison_set: the stocks analysed by the new approach (the Sets of Questions/Items approach)
rule.fixed_letters: on memo topics 5, 6, 8, 11 and 12 a cell carrying fixed_letter shows the Rater's own letter from a real-world measure (A to F, no sub-grade), never re-cut; its rank and p are information only (D-SQ-267, D-SQ-271)

RANK within the population of stocks scored on the same scale (A top 10%; B next 15%, B+ its top half; C next 25% in thirds C+, C, C-; D next 25%; F bottom 25%) for the judgement items. rule.scales: v1.5: every cell carries scale_tag; a rank letter is cut only among cells of the same scale (rater-v3 = the Rater v3.0 after the memo; rater-v2 and rater-v1-keyed = earlier Raters; writer-1.9 = the Investment Analyst's own score as it wrote the answer, the old method; writer-memo = the memo Analyst's own topic score). rule.scale_caveat: scores tagged rater-v1-keyed were set by the Rater of 1-Nov-26, whose key put 50 at the typical listed European company but was anchored on effect size rather than on percentiles; scores tagged rater-v2 or rater-v3 are standings in the Universe.
